questions.question: A 248-m-long train travelling at 88 km/h takes 30 seconds to cross another train, x m long, travelling at 34 km/h in the same direction. What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Length of first train = 248 m

length of second train = x m

Speed of first train = 88 km/h

Speed of second train = 34 km/h

Time = 30 second

**Formula Used**

Relative speed of train = (Speed of first train - speed of second train)

when trains are moving in same direction

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation**

Relative speed = (88 - 34) km/h

54 km/h

⇒ (54 × 1000)/(60 × 60) m/s

⇒ 15 m/s

Total distance travelled by train = 248 + x

Time = (248 + x)/15

⇒ 30 = (248 + x)/15

⇒ 450 = 248 + x

⇒ x = 450 - 248

⇒ x = 202 m

**∴ Length of second train is 202 m long.**

questions.question: A trader marks his goods in such a way that after allowing 16% discount on the marked price, he still gains 26%. If the cost price of the goods is Rs. 318, then what is the marked price of the goods?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of Cost Price (CP) to Marked Price (MP) can be written directly as (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%).

CP : MP = (100 − 16) : (100 + 26) = 84 : 126 = 2 : 3.

Here, 2 units represent the given CP = Rs. 318.

So, 1 unit = 318 ÷ 2 = Rs. 159.

Therefore, the Marked Price (3 units) = 159 × 3 = Rs. 477.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 477.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 318

Discount% = 16%

Profit% = 26%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 CP
 Rs. 318

 
 SP

 
 MP
 ?

 

 +26% Profit

 

 -16% Disc

 

 Ratio CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = CP + (26% of CP)

⇒ SP = 318 × (100 + 26) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 318 × 1.26 = 400.68

⇒ SP = MP − (16% of MP)

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 16) ÷ 100

⇒ 400.68 = MP × 0.84

⇒ MP = 400.68 ÷ 0.84

⇒ MP = 477

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 477.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP to MP Relationship

The most efficient way to link CP, MP, Profit, and Discount is using the ratio: CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − a×b÷100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit% = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

questions.question: The average score of A, B and C in a test is 78 and that of C, D and E is 52. The average score of E and F is 48 and that of E and C is 60. What is the average score of A, B, C, D, E and F?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average score of A, B and C is 78

Average score of C, D and E IS 52.

Average score of E and F is 48

Average score of E and C is 60

**Concept **

Average = Sum of all observationover Number of observation

**Calculation**

**{(A + B + C)}over{3}** = 78

 ⇒ A + B + C = 234

(C + D + E)over3 = 52

⇒ C + D + E = 156. ---- (1)

(E + F)over2 = 48

E + F = 96

⇒ E = 96 - F. ---- (2)

(E + C)over2 = 60

E + C = 120

⇒ E = 120 - C. ---- (3)

From (2) and (3)

96 - F = 120 - C

⇒ 96 - 120 = - C + F

⇒ F + 24 = C. ---- (4)

From (1) and (4)

F + 24 + D + 96 - F = 156

⇒ D = 156 - 120

⇒ D = 36

A + B + C = 234

D = 36

E + F = 96

So, Average of A,B,C,D E and F = (234 + 36 + 96)over6

⇒ 366over6

⇒ 61

**∴ The average score of A, B, C, D, E and F is 61.**

questions.question: Anu sells articles A and B for Rs. 4,000 each, with no loss or profit in the entire transaction. If A is sold at a 25% profit, then B is sold at a loss of:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of article A and B = 4000 each

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Cost price + Profit, when C.P S.P

Loss% = (loss/cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Selling price of article A and B together = Rs. 8000

let the cost price of article A = Rs. x

Selling price of article A = x + 25% of x

4000 = 125x/100

x = (4000 × 100)/125

x = Rs.3200

Cost price of article A = Rs. 3200

As there is no profit or loss in the entire transactions. so, cost price is equal to selling price.

Cost price of article B = Rs.(8000 - 3200)

⇒ Rs.4800

Selling price of article B = Rs.4000

Loss = Rs 4800 - Rs. 4000

⇒ Rs. 800

Loss % = (800/4800) × 100

⇒ 16{2over3} 

**∴ B is sold at a loss of 16{2over 3} %**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Total SP = Rs. 8000 and Total CP = Rs. 8000

CP of 2ⁿd articles = Rs. (8000 – 3200) = Rs. 4800

SP of 2ⁿd articles = Rs. 4000

∴ Loss on 2ⁿd articles = (800/4800 × 100)

⇒ 50/3 = 16{2over3}

**∴ **B is sold at a loss of 16{2over 3} %.

questions.question: Three years ago, the average age of A, B and C was 29 years. If the average age of B and C, 5 years ago, was 23 years, then what is the present age (in years) of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present average of A, B, and C = 29 + 3 = 32 years.

Present sum of ages of A, B, and C = 32 × 3 = 96 years.

Present average of B and C = 23 + 5 = 28 years.

Present sum of ages of B and C = 28 × 2 = 56 years.

Present age of A = 96 − 56 = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of A, B, and C, 3 years ago = 29 years

Average age of B and C, 5 years ago = 23 years

**Formula Used:**

Sum of ages = Average age × Number of persons

 Present Age Sum Distribution
 
 
 Sum of Present Ages of A, B, C = 96
 
 
• 
 

 
 
 Sum of B, C = 56
 
 
 Age of A = 40
 
 +

 A = 96 − 56 = 40 years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ages of A, B, and C (3 years ago) = 29 × 3 = 87 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of A, B, and C = 87 + (3 persons × 3 years) = 87 + 9 = 96 years

⇒ Sum of ages of B and C (5 years ago) = 23 × 2 = 46 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of B and C = 46 + (2 persons × 5 years) = 46 + 10 = 56 years

⇒ Present age of A = (Present sum of A, B, and C) − (Present sum of B and C)

⇒ Present age of A = 96 − 56 = 40 years

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Change in Average

If every individual value in a group increases by 'k' years (like aging), then the average of the group also increases by exactly 'k' years.

Combined Group Value

The sum of elements in a larger group minus the sum of elements in its subset will always yield the sum of the remaining uncounted elements.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of any two persons remains constant throughout their lifetime, regardless of past or future progression.
</p
